depth_findings.text: DeleteThreadWorkspace takes thread_id and org_id from the request body and authz grants write to any user principal, so S5 must derive the owner from the principal or a lease before erasing; it is Unimplemented now, so there is no exposure yet.
threadworkspace Store.Apply and Get SQL (row lock, upsert, delete, revision) run only in the integration test, which has not been executed against Postgres.
No concurrency test for two simultaneous Apply calls on one thread; the header row lock is the only guard for quota and revision.
Migration 0006 fails on a database with duplicate live thread leases; the check in lead_todo must be run before applying it.
ApplyThreadWorkspaceChanges accepts any non-empty content_hash; format sha256:<hex> is not validated at the boundary.
GetThreadWorkspace writes last_used_at on every read, one extra UPDATE per read; acceptable for retention but worth measuring.
No per-file size cap in the server (the 8 MiB exclusion belongs to WS22-S2 sync); only file count and total bytes are capped.
Thread leases have no expiry sweeper; expired thread leases stay in the table until S5 or S6 add lifecycle handling.
The zdr flag is honoured only for thread scope; a zdr=true agent-scope acquire is accepted as before, which is correct today because only thread scope carries workspace state.

A thread-scoped AcquireLease that names a space_id is still accepted while the switch is off (pre-WS22 path), and the row it creates sits in the leases_thread_live_uq index; after the switch is turned on, AcquireThread upserts onto that row and every thread RPC for that thread returns FailedPrecondition until it expires. Refuse thread scope with a non-empty space_id before the switch branch, or exclude space_id<>'' rows from the index predicate.

threadworkspace.checkPath accepts "." (path.Clean(".") == "." and it is not rejected), so a thread file named "." is stored; S2 hydration would then target the workspace root. Reject "." and add it to TestPlanChangesRefusesPathsThatEscapeOrRepeat before the switch can be on.

The ZDR refusal exists only at acquire. threadLease, GetThreadWorkspace and ApplyThreadWorkspaceChanges take no zdr input, so a holder of a non-ZDR thread lease id can still read and write thread rows. S2 must refuse ZDR at workspace open and commit as well as at acquire, and a test should pin it.

Store.Get reads the files and the revision in two statements outside a transaction, so a concurrent Apply can return files from a newer revision than the one reported. Read both in one REPEATABLE READ transaction or a single query.

AcquireThread's ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE does not refresh backend_id, so after SANDBOX_MANAGER_BACKEND_ID changes an acquire returns the old backend and later thread RPCs fail with BackendMismatch until expiry; this should be stated or handled.

Missing tests: the strict parser threadWorkspaceEnabled in cmd/main.go; a thread RPC on an expired lease; a ZDR-flagged Get/Apply path; a concurrent Apply on one thread; a batch with an unbounded number of changes (only resulting file count and bytes are capped, the gRPC 4 MiB limit is the only bound).

A mistyped SANDBOX_MANAGER_THREAD_WORKSPACE (for example True or yes) silently leaves the switch off with no log line; it fails safe, but the plan says strict true/false, so warn or refuse at startup for any non-empty value other than true or false.
GetThreadWorkspace writes last_used_at on every read, adding one UPDATE per read; the retention sweeper needs it, but the cost should be measured in S5.

DeleteThreadWorkspace is authorised for any write-scope principal and takes thread_id and org_id from the body; when S5 implements it, derive the owner from the principal or lease, as the implementer noted.
Thread leases have no expiry sweeper and no lifecycle handling; expired rows stay in the live index until S5 or S6.

In internal/lease/lease.go the AcquireThread doc comment is glued to the stray lookup doc comment lines ("participates in the WHERE clause...") that were left above it, so the godoc for AcquireThread carries lookup's text.
